summary: Allan's Island Lighthouse at Lamaline, Burin Peninsula: a wooden octagon of 1879 (or 1880), then iron, then a 2004 tower. Listed staffed in a 2005 DFO brochure; grounds open, tower closed.

structures.note: Octagonal wooden tower, sides painted alternately red and white (LighthouseFriends); removed 1916 per LighthouseFriends
Round cast-iron tower (LighthouseFriends: 1916; Rowlett: replaced in 1920); replaced by the 1953 tower
Square pyramidal wooden tower, thirty feet tall (LighthouseFriends); replaced around 2004
Present white tower with red top (Coast Guard list). LighthouseFriends and Rowlett both say erected around 2004

staffing.note: Listed among the staffed lightstations in the Fisheries and Oceans Canada brochure DFO/2005-167 (copyright 2005). The Fisheries and Oceans web page reads 'Date modified: 2019-09-24', which is a web-page date, not a staffing date

access.note: Listed as a staffed lightstation (DFO brochure, 2005), so the keepers' home is a working place. Grounds open, tower closed (LighthouseFriends; Rowlett). Reached by a road that crosses a causeway to the island.

events.note: Work began on the lighthouse on Allan's Island, after a 1877 petition to the Newfoundland House of Assembly (LighthouseFriends)
LighthouseFriends: first lit 1879. Rowlett gives station established 1880
Small structure with a sleeping room for the keeper added beside the tower
John Fleming appointed after Keeper John Messervey died in September 1885
Upgraded to a fourth-order dioptric light
Range lights on poles at Lamaline: front light 6.6 m on the shore, rear light 146 m inland at 10 m
Octagonal wooden tower removed after an iron tower and new dwelling were built. LighthouseFriends gives 1916; Rowlett gives 1920 for the round cast-iron tower
Fog alarm powered by compressed air from an oil engine; two blasts every ninety seconds
Two enclosed square pyramidal range towers replaced the pole range lights. LighthouseFriends gives 1926; Rowlett gives 1927
Square pyramidal wooden tower, thirty feet tall, and a double keepers' dwelling built beside it

corrections.why: The record's first-light year is Rowlett's station-established year. LighthouseFriends says the light was first lit in 1879. The Coast Guard list gives no date. A human should confirm which year the editor wants shown as first lit.

notes_for_editor: Thin on primary sources. Every 1877-1953 fact comes from LighthouseFriends, which cites the Journal of the House of Assembly of Newfoundland; those journals are on MUN's Digital Archives (collections.mun.ca) and were not read, so the petition and the 1890 inspection are LighthouseFriends' account. The Canadian Marine reports in the corpus do not cover this light (Newfoundland was not in Canada until 1949). Date conflicts left open: first light 1879 (LighthouseFriends) against 1880 (Rowlett, station established); iron tower 1916 against 1920; range towers 1926 against 1927. Keeper names and dates come only from LighthouseFriends' list; William Cake has no dates. Keepers from 1964 on (Lawrence Slaney) are named only as the published list names them, public role only. The Coast Guard list gives the range as 16 nm; MarineRadar's 13 NM was not used. The 'staffed' status: the Fisheries and Oceans Canada brochure (DFO/2005-167, copyright 2005) names the station on its staffed list. Its web page reads 'Date modified: 2019-09-24', a web-page date, not a status date, so no source read gives current staffing. Wikipedia's Allan's Island article was read for leads only and not cited.
